title: Handoff Verification API PRD Sketch
summary: Sketch for a compact Handoff Verification API to provide deterministic proofs and audit traces when a customer-managed network or operator action hands control back to Redwood Private. Focus: signed compact evidence, async approval gates, and playback-friendly audit streams.
background: Customers running Private deployments require a small, machine-verifiable interface for cross-boundary operations: e.g., when a tenant operator applies a VPC change, hands a snapshot to Redwood, or when we need cryptographic proof of an on-prem attestation. Existing proposals focus on large immutable ledgers and heavy attestation artifacts; this sketch aims for a pragmatic API and compact evidence envelope for common handoff flows and audits.
goals: 1) Define minimal API surface for initiating, verifying, and replaying handoffs; 2) Design a compact attestation envelope (CAE) format suitable for bandwidth-constrained networks; 3) Specify audit retention tiers and sampling semantics tied to approval gates; 4) Provide integration guidance for operator agents and customer orchestration scripts.
non_goals: 1) Replace customer full forensic exports (we expect customers to retain raw logs); 2) Define cryptographic key management best-practices in detail (assume KMS/HSM integration points exist); 3) Build full UI — this doc is API + telemetry + rollout patterns only.
user_stories:
- As a platform ops engineer, I want Redwood to be able to verify that a tenant's VPC snapshot corresponds to the signed snapshot I uploaded so Redwood can safely accept an inbound connection.
- As a security auditor, I want a compact, replayable evidence artifact I can hand to compliance for incident triage.
- As a customer SRE, I want to gate sensitive changes with a canary approval that produces verifiable audit records for future rollback.
high_level_flow: 1) Operator prepares a snapshot and generates CAE with ephemeral nonce and signed metadata. 2) Operator calls /v1/handoff/initiate, uploads CAE or CAE pointer. 3) Redwood validates signature, verifies nonce freshness, and returns tentative handoff-id. 4) If change requires approval gate, an 'approval token' is issued and routed to configured approvers (can be automated or human). 5) On approval, /v1/handoff/complete is called and the CAE becomes part of Redwood's compact audit stream. 6) /v1/handoff/replay allows sanitized playback for audits.
api_contract_proposals:
- POST /v1/handoff/initiate: body: CAE or CAE URL, metadata (tenant_id, change_type, seq, ttl). Returns handoff_id and status: pending|accepted|requires_approval.
- GET /v1/handoff/status/{handoff_id}: returns validation state, approver list, audit keys.
- POST /v1/handoff/approve/{handoff_id}: accepts approval token + signer info; can be automation or user.
- POST /v1/handoff/complete/{handoff_id}: finalizes and emits compact audit record.
- GET /v1/handoff/replay/{handoff_id}?format=log|summary: returns playback artifact with redaction hints.
- Webhook: /v1/handoff/events for async notifications (approved/failed/expired).
compact_attestation_format: CAE (Compact Attestation Envelope) - top-level fields: version, issuer, subject, nonce, timestamp, change_manifest_digest, optional payload pointer, signature(s). CAE must be small (<16KB typical) but allow payload pointers into customer-managed object stores for large artifacts. Signatures should support multiple signers (operator + attester). Use COSE or compact JWS encoding as implementation options.
telemetry_and_audit:
- Event model: handoff.initiated, handoff.validated, handoff.requires_approval, handoff.approved, handoff.completed, handoff.replayed, handoff.expired.
- Each event emits structured fields: handoff_id, tenant_id, change_type, validator_version, validation_notes, approver_ids.
- Retention tiers: ephemeral (7d), compliance (90d), long-term (365d encrypted archive). Customers select tier at initiation or via tenant policy.
- Sampling: for high-frequency automated approvals, default sampling 1% full payload + 100% compact metadata; allow customer opt-in for higher fidelity.
- Replay knobs: redact_level (none|partial|full) and include_signatures boolean.
approval_gate_matrix:
- Low-risk: auto-approve if CAE signatures valid and change manifests within whitelisted ranges.
- Medium-risk: require 1 human approver OR automated validation job success.
- High-risk: require 2 human approvers from distinct groups; emit sticky evidence to long-term retention.
- Escalation: failed auto-validate routes to oncall via webhook and creates a pending ticket (linkable to RD-9742).
security_considerations:
- Nonce replay protection: handoff_id + server-side nonce cache with TTL.
- Signature verification must support customer KMS roots; Redwood should provide a plug for customer public keys and freshness checks.
- Minimal PII in CAE: recommend hashing sensitive fields and storing pointer to customer store for full objects.
- Rate limiting and abuse detection for initiate endpoints.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: internal prototype and test harness (unit validations + local operator).
Phase 1: invite-only beta with 3 customers (focus on VPC snapshots and operator handoff).
Phase 2: public beta, sampling defaults enabled, telemetry dashboards added to Console.
Phase 3: GA with SLA for evidence availability and retention options.
Instrumentation: per-handoff latency, validation error breakdown, approval latency percentiles.
open_questions:
- CAE canonical encoding: COSE vs compact JWS? Need crypto team input.
- Retention legal boundaries: do we need region-specific defaults per customer jurisdiction? Legal to advise.
- Should approvals be modeled as separate resources to be reused across handoffs? (replay/rollbacks)
- Do we require mandatory SIEM forwarding for high-risk buckets? (integration with customer SIEMs).
